answer: Trust propagates from trusted seeds through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, with per-identity voting caps. If a sybil cluster—whether labeled zephyr, sonnet, or dune—has few edges to honest nodes, its low conductance limits walk flow across that boundary; min-cut bounds then constrain how much independent trusted support, and thus aggregate voting weight, it can acquire. This bound depends on seed placement and walk length, not cluster size alone.
